subject: microbiology
title: Bacterial Genetics III: VRE, Molecular Diagnostics and Susceptibility Testing

steps.tx: **VRE** (vancomycin resistant enterococci) rewires peptidoglycan precursors from D Ala D Ala to D Ala D Lac (vanA, vanB operons on transposons and plasmids), collapsing vancomycin binding a thousand fold, mostly in Enterococcus faecium, answering with linezolid and daptomycin (dose and syndrome dependent). Vancomycin's glycopeptide target from the pharmacology lessons is literally rebuilt by the resistance operon.
steps.say: VRE changes the wall's last two amino acids and vancomycin loses its grip.

left.title: van operons
points: vanB: variable level, teicoplanin often susceptible
vanC: intrinsic low level in E gallinarum group
D Ala D Lac reduces binding about 1000 fold

right.title: VRE practice
points: Rectal screening in high risk units
Linezolid and daptomycin therapy by syndrome

steps.tx: **PCR** (polymerase chain reaction) amplifies target DNA through denaturation, primer annealing and extension cycles into detectable millions, real time formats quantifying as they go (Ct values), multiplex panels naming respiratory, meningitis, gastrointestinal and bloodstream pathogens in hours. Its sensitivity creates the colonisation versus infection questions that clinical correlation must answer.
steps.say: Thirty cycles make a billion copies; the clinician still decides if copies mean disease.

left.title: PCR mechanics
points: Real time fluorescence: Ct inversely grades quantity
Reverse transcription first for RNA viruses

right.title: PCR cautions
points: Inhibitors in stool and blood cause false negatives
Negative never overrides strong clinical syndromes alone

steps.tx: **PCR** copies a chosen DNA target through repeating cycles of denaturation, primer annealing, and extension until millions of copies can be detected. Real time formats measure product as it forms and report a cycle threshold. Multiplex panels name respiratory, meningitis, gastrointestinal, and bloodstream pathogens in hours rather than days of culture. Sensitivity this high also detects colonisation and leftover nucleic acid. A positive curve therefore starts a clinical question rather than ending it. The clinician still has to decide whether those copies explain the illness in front of them.
steps.say: PCR cycles through denaturation, annealing, and extension until a DNA target becomes detectable. Real time assays report a cycle threshold as product accumulates. Multiplex panels identify respiratory, gut, meningitis, and bloodstream pathogens within hours. Because colonisation also yields copies, the curve does not by itself prove disease.

vis.alt: Real time amplification curves rise across cycles, with cycle threshold marks where each sample crosses the detection line.
vis.caption: Amplification curves climb after denaturation, annealing, and extension, and the cycle threshold shows when product becomes detectable. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **DNA probes and sequencing** extend identification beyond culture: hybridisation probes from colonies (historical), MALDI's protein cousin already met, 16S rRNA sequencing naming uncultured or fastidious bacteria from tissue, and whole genome sequencing arbitrating outbreaks and resistance genes in reference laboratories. Each method trades speed, cost and resolution against the culture it increasingly accompanies rather than replaces.
steps.say: Sequence the universal gene when culture stays silent; genome the outbreak when typing blurs.

left.title: Identification ladder
points: Whole genome: outbreaks and resistance prediction

right.title: Syndromic panels
points: Blood culture identification panels after flag
Positive panel still needs phenotypic susceptibility

steps.tx: **Antimicrobial susceptibility testing** converts a name into a prescription: disc diffusion (Kirby Bauer) grading zones against breakpoints, dilution MICs in broth or agar, gradient strips marrying the two, reported as susceptible, intermediate (susceptible increased exposure in modern EUCAST language) or resistant by CLSI and EUCAST standards recalibrated as pharmacology evolves.
steps.say: A zone diameter is a prescription in disguise, translated by breakpoint committees.

left.title: Kirby Bauer
points: Fast, cheap, robust for routine drugs

right.title: MIC methods
points: MIC guides vancomycin, aminoglycoside and salvage dosing

steps.tx: **Antimicrobial susceptibility testing** turns an organism name into a drug choice. In the Kirby Bauer disc diffusion method, zone diameters are read against published breakpoints. Broth or agar dilution gives a minimum inhibitory concentration directly. Gradient strips combine a concentration ramp with a zone like reading. Results are reported as susceptible, intermediate, or resistant. Modern EUCAST language often renames intermediate as susceptible at increased exposure. CLSI and EUCAST recalibrate those cut offs as pharmacology changes, so a zone is never interpreted from memory of an old chart alone.
steps.say: Kirby Bauer disc diffusion grades zone diameters against breakpoints. Dilution methods give a minimum inhibitory concentration, and gradient strips blend both ideas. Reports say susceptible, intermediate, or resistant. EUCAST may call intermediate susceptible at increased exposure. CLSI and EUCAST move the cut offs as drug pharmacology is updated.

vis.alt: A culture plate shows antibiotic discs surrounded by clear zones of inhibition of different diameters.
vis.caption: Zone diameters around discs are compared with breakpoints and reported as susceptible, intermediate, or resistant. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The **MIC** (minimum inhibitory concentration, lowest drug level stopping visible growth) and MBC (bactericidal, killing 99.9 percent) frame dosing philosophy: time above MIC for beta lactams, peak and AUC ratios for aminoglycosides and fluoroquinolones from the pharmacology lessons. Breakpoints fuse MIC distributions, pharmacokinetics and outcomes, which is why the same MIC can be susceptible for one site and resistant for meningitis.
steps.say: MIC is a number; breakpoint is that number judged by site, dose and outcome.

left.title: Reading MICs
points: Lower is more susceptible, scale is doubling
ECOFF separates wild type from acquired resistance
Cidal versus static by MBC ratio niches

right.title: Site corrections
points: Urinary only agents reported for urine isolates
Expert rules suppress misleading susceptible results

steps.tx: **Phenotypic resistance confirmations** remain molecular testing's referees: D test for inducible clindamycin resistance in staphylococci, ESBL clavulanate synergy, carbapenemase inhibitor and hydrolysis tests, methicillin cefoxitin screening, and vancomycin screening agars for VRE. A resistance gene found without expression, or expressed without the gene panel's target, both occur often enough to keep phenotypes employed.
steps.say: Genes predict, phenotypes confess; report both when they disagree, phenotype leads therapy.

left.title: Phenotypic classics
points: D zone test flattens toward clindamycin

right.title: Discordance handling
points: Gene positive, phenotype susceptible: expert review
Phenotype resistant, panel negative: novel mechanism hunt
Infection control acts on either signal

steps.tx: **Antibiogram and cumulative susceptibility** reporting turns thousands of isolate results into empirical therapy policy (first isolate per patient, annual, unit specific where numbers allow), the stewardship committee's map from which empirical guidelines in this curriculum's pharmacology lessons are drawn. Genetics gave mechanisms; antibiograms give local probabilities.
steps.say: Prescribe empirically from your own hospital's map, not another continent's textbook table.

nodes.label: Percent susceptible by organism and unit
Empirical guidelines written from the map
Outcomes and resistance trends reviewed yearly

steps.tx: **Molecular window discipline** closes the genetics module: nucleic acid tests still need viable organism recovery for susceptibility in most bacterial disease, contamination and colonisation literacy in interpreting panels, and retention of isolates for typing when outbreaks declare later. Culture is slower and remains the only method that hands you the organism itself.
steps.say: Keep the isolate; tomorrow's outbreak question needs the organism, not its Ct value.
